 Order:

1. Complainant Kuldeep has filed present revision petition challenging the impugned order dated 04.02.2023 whereby Ld. MM(Mahila Court)-05 West had discharged all the accused persons for Kuldeep vs State on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73049168/
1 offences u/s 498A/406/34 IPC.
2.
The Respondents no. 2 and 3 in the present revision petition are the accused persons who were chargesheeted before Ld. Trial Court in case FIR No. 445-2016, PS Ranhola.
State has been impleaded as Respondent no.1 in the present revision petition.
For the sake of convenience, parties shall be referred to by their nomenclature before Ld. Trial Court.
3. Arguments on the revision petition have been heard.
Record carefully perused.
BRIEF FACTS 4.

Brief facts of the case necessary for disposing off the present revision petition are that the present FIR was registered on the basis of a complaint dated 11.06.2016 made by complainant Kuldeep against the in laws of her deceased sister Kavita.
As per the chargesheet, Kavita (since deceased) was married to accused Amit Kumar on 09.03.2015.
Sufficient dowry articles were given in her marriage.
At that time, Kavita (since deceased) was working as a Staff Nurse in RBI PMT Hospital and was an employee of MCD, Delhi Government.
She was earning a salary of about Rs. 55000/- to Rs. 60000/-.
However, after her marriage her entire salary was taken by accused Amit and his parents and she was given a meagre sum of Rs. 2000/- as pocket money in a month.

In addition,
accused Amit and his parents used to taunt her for bringing insufficient dowry and low quality products in dowry.

Complainant and his family members were also taunted by mother of accused Amit Kumar namely Late Smt. Meena Devi stating that their son was well educated and if he was married somewhere else, he would have receive a four wheeler in dowry.
Parents of accused Amit taunted the family members of the complainant for being poor and made demands of dowry and car.
Because of all these reasons, Kavita (since deceased) was mentally disturbed.
When Kavita conceived a child, she was not given proper attention.
She wanted her treatment from a good hospital, however, her in- laws did not listen to her and took her to Asha Hospital, Vikas Nagar for check-up.
Kavita was not given proper diet and was continuously taunted by her mother-in-law Late Smt. Meena Devi.
Kavita (since deceased) was admitted in Asha Hospital on 05.06.2016 in morning hours for delivery.
She delivered a baby girl by cesarean on 05.06.2016 at 5.30 pm.
However, she was not properly cared for after delivery and was left alone.
Kavita wanted to get the chord (stem cell) of the child preserve but it was not permitted by her in-laws.
Since, she was not properly cared for after delivery, on 07.06.2016 in the evening hours, her condition deteriorated and she started having vomiting.
Still, accused Amit and his parents did not shift her to a better hospital.
When her condition could not be controlled, she was shifted to Orchid Hospital, Janakpuri, however, she expired on 08.06.2016 at about 12.12 am.
Complainant alleged that accused Amit, his father accused Saheb Singh and his mother Late Smt. Meena Devi were responsible for the death of Kavita.
He also stated that in case hospital staff was found negligent, legal action should be initiated against them also.

On the basis of this complaint, present FIR was registered u/s 498A/304A/34 IPC on 11.06.2016.
5. During investigation, postmortem of the deceased Kavita was conducted on 11.06.2016 and the final opinion regarding the cause of her death was kept pending till receipt of viscera chemical analysis report and histopathalogical examination report.

After obtaining the said report, final Kuldeep vs State on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73049168/
2 opinion regarding the cause of death was given by the Autopsy Surgeon vide his final report dated 15.07.2016 wherein it was opined that the cause of death was anemia induced by pregnancy and aggravated by complication of surgical delivery of fetus.

sentences.text: IO recorded statement of the witnesses u/s 161 CrPC and after completion of investigation, filed the charge-sheet u/s 498A/406/34 IPC without arrest against accused Amit Kumar (husband of deceased) and Saheb Singh (father-in-law of deceased).

Abated charge-sheet was filed against Smt. Meena Devi (mother-in-law of deceased),
who had expired during investigation.
6.
Proceedings qua accused Smt. Meena Devi were abated vide order dated 29.05.2019.
Other accused persons were summoned by Ld. Trial Court after taking cognizance of the offences vide order dated 29.05.2019.
Complainant also appeared before Ld. Trial Court on 15.10.2019.

A quashing petition was filed by the accused persons but since no stay in the matter was received, Ld.
Trial Court proceeded further with the trial of the case.

IMPUGNED ORDER:
7.

After hearing the arguments on the point of charge, Ld. Trial Court discharged all the accused persons holding that considering the investigation done, material on record, the final opinion regarding cause of death, statements u/s 161 CrPC recorded by the IO, there were no specific allegations against any of the accused persons nor any single incident had been narrated by the complainant making out a reasonably prima facie case u/s 498A/406/34 IPC against the accused persons.
There are no allegations of entrustment of any articles of the deceased to any accused persons nor there are any allegations of any misappropriation done by them.

Ld. Trial Court also observed that Sec. 304A IPC initially attracted at the time of registration of the FIR was removed considering the medical evidence that came on record regarding the cause of death of deceased Kavita.

Accordingly, both the accused persons were discharged for offences under Sec.
498A/406/34 IPC vide impugned order dated 04.02.2023.
GROUNDS OF REVISION / ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF COMPLAINANT 8.

In the present revision petition, complainant has challenged the impugned order on the ground that the impugned order dated 04.02.2023 discharging the accused persons has been passed in a hurry without giving proper opportunity to the complainant to address the arguments.

Ld. Trial Court had failed to appreciate that there has been negligible investigation by the concerned IO in the present case and the charge-sheet was not filed under appropriate and applicable sections of IPC.

Complainant was forced to file a separate complaint case under Sec. 156(3) Cr.PC vide CC No.
1009/2017 which was adjudicated by Ld. MM-08, West and finally a charge-sheet was filed against the accused persons.

Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate true facts of the case and the allegations made in the complaint regarding active intentional negligence of the accused persons in taking care of deceased Kavita immediately after birth of the girl child through cesarean operation as well as the allegations that accused persons were continuously harassing deceased Kavita for not bringing sufficient and good quality dowry articles.

The allegations in the complaint that the accused persons kept on demanding other articles and the family members of complainant fulfilled their unreasonable demands have been ignored by Ld. Trial Court.

Ld. Trial Court also failed to Kuldeep vs State on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73049168/
3 appreciate that accused had misrepresented himself as working as a Faculty with Engineering College, Roorkee and earning a handsome salary of Rs. 50,000/- per month although he was unemployed.

sentences.text: 9. Ld. Trial Court also failed to appreciate that deceased Kavita had nominated her mother as her nominee for all her benefits, savings, investment etc., with her employer and bank, which nomination was not changed by her during her life time and she was also harassed on this account.

Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that immediately after demise of Kavita, accused persons filed a petition for grant of succession certificate for claiming the terminal benefit, savings, investments etc., of deceased Kavita without naming the mother of the deceased despite being aware of the fact that she was a named nominee.

Ld. Trial Court had failed to appreciate that immediately after birth of girl child, deceased Kavita was abandoned by accused persons in ill equipped Asha Hospital and this was the reason why her condition deteriorated.

Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that after the demise of Kavita, accused Amit had fled away from the hospital with the new born child and did not even receive the dead body for performing last rites.
Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that accused Amit Kumar is a habitual offender of domestic violence and abuse to his wives and has already married four times.
Accordingly, it is submitted that the impugned order is bad in law and deserves to be set aside.
ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF ACCUSED PERSONS:
10. Per contra, the accused persons have supported the impugned order stating that it is a well reasoned order based on material available on record.
There is no infirmity and illegality in the impugned order.

All the allegations made in the complaint have been carefully perused by Ld. Trial Court while passing the impugned order and it has been rightly held that there are no specific allegations against any of the accused persons.
Perusal of the complaint dated 09.06.2016 shows that it does not mention even a single incident of dowry demand made by any of the accused persons to substantiate the allegations of Section 498A IPC.
The allegations are vague without any date, time or place.
Moreover, there are no allegations of any entrustment of any dowry articles by deceased Kavita to any of the accused persons.

In addition to this, charge-sheet was never filed under Sec.
304A IPC for death by negligence as no evidence in this regard was found and the cause of death was opined to the anemia induced by pregnancy and aggravated by complications of the surgical delivery of fetus.
Most of the grounds in the present revision petition taken by the complainant are imaginary and do not find any mention in the charge-sheet.
There is no evidence on record to support the contention of the complainant that accused Amit Kumar is a habitual offender with respect to domestic violence or has solemnized four marriages.
Again, there is no evidence on record that the accused was neglected after her delivery.
No such evidence has been collected during the investigation.
Again there is no evidence to show that Asha Hospital was an ill equipped hospital not suitable for delivery.
Admittedly, deceased Kavita was a nurse by profession and therefore, it cannot be presumed that she had got herself admitted in ill equipped hospital for the purpose of delivery.
The allegations made in the present revision petition are nothing but a fragment of imagination of a brother who is distressed due to the demise of his sister.
However, merely because Kavita had expired due to her medical conditions, the accused persons cannot be blamed or made liable for her demise.

sentences.text: In addition to this, the complainant himself had admitted that he had filed an application under Sec. 156(3) Cr.PC for expediting the investigation of the case and the said application and its record is already annexed with the Trial Court record.
Perusal of the same clearly show that the complainant was well aware about the fact that the charge-sheet was filed under Sec. 498A/406/34 IPC and Sec. 304A IPC was dropped during investigation.
However, he did not prefer to file any protest petition against the said charge-sheet nor he pressed for framing of charges under the said section.

He had been continuously appearing before the Ld Trial Court since 15.10.2019 and thus, he cannot claim that he was not given opportunity to argue the matter or that the impugned order discharging the accused persons has been passed in haste.
In these circumstances, it is submitted that there is no merit in the present revision petition.
Accordingly, dismissal of the present revision petition is sought.
ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE 12.
On behalf of the State, Ld. Additional PP has also supported the impugned order dated 04.02.2023.
It is submitted that it is a well reasoned order passed on the basis of allegations made in the complaint and material collected during investigation.
There is no infirmity or illegality in the same and there is no reason for interfering with the impugned order dated 04.02.2024, hence dismissal of the present revision petition is sought.

FINDINGS:
13. I have heard the submissions made and carefully perused the record.
14. The scope of enquiry, a judge is required to make while considering the question of framing of charges has been considered by the Apex Court in Union of India Vs.
Prafulla Kumar Samal and Anr. (1979) 3 SCC 4.

entities.text:
Union of India Vs.
Prafulla Kumar Samal and Anr. (1979) 3 SCC 4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
After an exhaustive survey of the case law on the point, the Apex court has laid down the following principles:-
" (1) That the Judge while considering the question of framing the charges under section 227 of the Code has the undoubted power to sift and weigh the evidence for the limited purpose of finding out whether or not a prima facie case against the accused has been made out.

(2) Where the materials placed before the Court disclose grave suspicion against the accused which has not been properly explained the Court will be, fully justified in framing a charge and proceeding with the trial.
(3) The test to determine a prima facie case would be naturally depend upon the facts of each case and it is difficult to lay down a rule of universal application.

By and large however, if two views are equally possible and the Judge is satisfied that the evidence produced before him while giving rise to some suspicion but not grave suspicion against the accused, he will be fully within his right to discharge the accused.
(4) That in exercising his jurisdiction under section 227 of the Code the Judge which under the present Code is a senior and experienced Judge cannot act merely as a Post Kuldeep vs State on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73049168/
5 Office or a mouth-piece of the prosecution, but has to consider the broad probabilities of the case, the total effect of the evidence and the documents produced before the Court, any basic infirmities appearing in the case and so on.

This however,
does not mean that the Judge should make a roving enquiry into the pros and cons of the matter and weigh the evidence as if he was conducting a trial."
15. Section 498A IPC provides punishment for cruelty to a woman by her husband or relative of her husband.
The term cruelty within the meaning of Section 498A IPC has been explained in the explanation to the said section.
It consists of two clauses (a) and (b).

To attract Section 498A IPC, it must be established that the cruelty or harassment to wife was to force her to cause grave bodily injury to herself or to commit suicide; or the harassment was to compel her to fulfill illegal demands of dowry.
Thus, every type of harassment or cruelty would not attract Section 498A IPC.

There are two essential ingredients for the offence of criminal breach of trust first being entrustment with property or dominion over property and the second is dishonest misappropriation of the property.
Both these ingredients are required to be present before an offence of criminal breach of trust punishable under Sec. 406 IPC can be held to be prima facie made out.
18. Sec. 304A IPC provides punishment for causing death by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide.

19. I have carefully perused the complaint on which present FIR has been registered as well as the documents annexed with the chargesheet and the statement of witnesses recorded u/s 161 CrPC.
20.
Considering the overall material available on record, no infirmity or illegality is found in the impugned order dated 04.02.2023 discharging the accused persons from the offences u/s 498A/406/34 IPC.

I find no infirmity or illegality in the reasoning given by Ld. Trial Court while discharging the accused persons as clearly no specific incident of dowry demand or harassment given to the sister of the complainant at the hands of any of the accused persons for fulfillment of Kuldeep vs State on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73049168/
6
the said dowry demands has been stated by the complainant in his complaint or by any of the relatives of the deceased in their statements recorded u/s 161 CrPC.
Neither any specific incident has been narrated nor there is any MLC of the sister of the complainant on record in respect of harassments given to her.
Thus, the essential ingredients for making a prima facie case u/s 498A IPC
are not reflected from the material available on record.

Mere allegations of taunts for bringing insufficient dowry or mere allegations of demand of four wheeler without corresponding allegations of harassment to the deceased for fulfillment of said dowry demands, are not sufficient for attracting offence under Sec. 498A IPC.
This is more so as in the present case, even these allegations are vague and without any date, month or year.

21. As regards offence under Sec. 406 IPC, clearly there is not even a single averment or evidence on record to show that any article belonging to the deceased was ever entrusted to any of the accused persons or has been misappropriated by them.
Thus, no prima facie case under Sec. 406 IPC is attracted against any of the accused persons.

22. As regards the contention of the complainant that he was not given proper opportunity to address arguments on the point of charge, it is found to be an incorrect submission as he was duly appearing either himself or through his counsel before Ld. Trial Court since 15.10.2019.
Arguments were also heard on his behalf on a date previous to passing of the impugned order as recorded in the ordersheet dated 05.11.2022.

Moreover, the averments made by the complainant in the present revision petition regarding the character of accused Amit Kumar, his subsequent marriages and his conduct after demise of deceased Kavita, the same are also irrelevant as no evidence in this regard is available in the record of Ld. Trial Court, which could have been considered by Ld. Trial Court.
23. Regarding the submissions of the complainant in respect of death of deceased Kavita due to negligence on behalf of the accused persons, again there is no corresponding evidence on record.

Howsoever aggrieved complainant may be due to demise of his sister, his suspicion alone cannot be made a basis for framing of charge against the accused persons blaming them for the death of his sister.
Record shows that offence under Sec. 304A IPC was dropped during investigation after receiving the final opinion regarding the cause of death as no malafides were found in the same.
The complainant was well aware about the dropping of the said offence since 21.08.2019 but he preferred not to file any protest petition or to bring any contrary evidence on record.
Accordingly at this stage, he cannot be permitted to reagitate the said issue.

24. Considering the overall material available on record and the reasons given by Ld. Trial Court in the impugned order dated 04.02.2023, I am of the opinion that the accused persons have been rightly discharged by Ld. Trial Court.

No infirmity or illegality is observed in the impugned order dated 04.02.2023.
25.
In view of the reasons given above, I find no merit in the present revision petition.
The same is accordingly, dismissed and the impugned order dated 04.02.2023 is upheld.
26. TCR be sent back along with a copy of this order.
